title: Make the viewer's start screen, runbooks and file references actionable

needs: The two hand-modelled demonstration assets live under the gitignored logics/external/modeles-3D/ -- fine for a personal machine, but the project itself has nowhere committed to keep them, so a fresh clone (or CI) never sees them.

The start screen's template cards show commands as plain, uncopiable-looking text with no way to run them, even when the page is served and could run some of them for real; and its three-column layout overflows its own modal on at least one screen width, the Environment column's long paths pushing past the right edge.

Opening the File menu, then clicking 'Start screen', leaves the File dropdown open and visible behind the splash modal it just opened -- a menu-closing check exists for clicks outside a menu, but the click that opens the splash originates from inside the menu, so that check never runs. (Fixed inline this session, in viewer.js's showSplash -- kept here as a Done slice so the whole pass has one record.)

A report's render panel and its Artefact section both show a ready-to-run 'blender <path>' command and a written file's path as plain selectable text, never as a button; the same is true of every other file path the viewer prints (runbook references, doc links, project paths in the Environment panel).

The runbook workspace's right-hand content pane renders a runbook's Markdown source as raw text -- headings, bullet lists and code fences all show their literal '##', '-' and backtick characters instead of being formatted.

The vehicle demonstration's glass panes (windshield and side/rear windows, thin single-quad Plane objects in the source asset) appear to be progressively lost across the demo chain's own operations -- not yet root-caused to a specific step.
context: adr_007 deliberately closed the set of commands a served page may run (list, doctor, prune) to a fixed, non-destructive set; build_demo_chain.sh and build_figurine_chain.sh are destructive by their own documented intent ('ponytail: destructive on this demonstration's project') and rebuild a whole sibling project from scratch, so adding them to that closed set is an architecture-level decision, not a UI tweak -- surfaced here for a decision, not pre-decided.

A file:// page has no server to reach and can only ever offer copy-to-clipboard for a command; an 'Open in Blender' affordance on a report's own artefact is a different, narrower case -- opening a local application on a local file the report already names, which a file:// page can offer via a plain file:// or blender:// style link without needing the /run endpoint at all, worth checking before assuming this needs the served-only path too.

Markdown rendering has to stay dependency-free like the rest of the viewer (adr_003/adr_004's no-framework, no-build-step stance) -- a small hand-rolled renderer covering headings, lists, code fences and links is in scope; pulling in a Markdown library is not.

The vehicle asset's glass panes are single-quad planes with very little volume of their own; scan_defects' coincident-duplicate removal, solidify's wall-or-skip decision, and voxel_remesh's shell-size floor are the three most likely places a nearly-zero-volume shell gets folded into another object or dropped outright -- named as starting points, not a diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Both hand-modelled assets are committed in the repository at a path outside logics/external/ (fixtures/ or equivalent), and both build scripts default to that committed copy first, ahead of the gitignored local one and the from-primitives generator.

AC2: The start screen's layout stays within its own modal at common desktop widths -- no column's content pushes past the modal's right edge -- verified by a rendered screenshot, not by inspection of the CSS alone.

AC3: A decision is recorded (a new or amended ADR, or an explicit non-goal) on whether the start screen's demo/figurine template commands become runnable from a served page, and the start screen matches whatever that decision is -- either real run buttons wired through an extended, still-closed command set, or the copy-to-clipboard behaviour kept deliberately and explained in the UI rather than left looking broken.

AC4: Every report-owned file path the viewer prints (the render panel's 'Open in Blender' command, the Artefact section's written-file path, runbook references, doc links) is a real clickable control -- a button that copies or runs per the file://-vs-served rule already established, or a link that opens the file directly where the platform allows it -- not plain unstyled text.

AC5: The runbook workspace renders a runbook's Markdown body as formatted HTML (headings, lists, code fences, links at minimum), with no literal Markdown syntax characters visible, using no new dependency.
AC6: The File-menu-stays-open-behind-the-splash defect is fixed and covered by the same viewer smoke suite so it cannot silently return.

AC7: The vehicle demonstration's glass-pane loss is root-caused to a specific operation and either fixed (the panes survive the full chain) or, if keeping them intact is not achievable without weakening a real lesson the chain teaches, documented honestly in the build script's comments and README -- not left unexplained.

product.title: A viewer that acts on what it shows, not just displays it
product.overview: Closes the gap between the viewer showing a command, a file path, or a runbook and the operator actually being able to act on it -- run it, open it, or read it formatted -- while keeping the viewer's no-framework, no-build-step, read-only-by-default character intact.
goals: The two hand-modelled demonstration assets are part of the committed project, not a personal local-only convenience.
The start screen is usable at common widths and honest about what its template commands can and cannot do from a served page.
Every file path and runnable command the viewer already prints is a real control, not text a person has to retype.
Runbook content is legible prose, not raw Markdown source.
The vehicle demonstration's glass panes survive the chain, or the chain is honest about why they don't.
non_goals: Extending the served page's command set to arbitrary shell commands; any addition stays closed and explicit, per adr_007.
A general Markdown library or a WYSIWYG editor; a small renderer covering this project's own runbook conventions is the target.
Reworking the viewer's overall layout system beyond fixing the specific overflow found.

backlog_items.title: Commit the two hand-modelled demo assets as project fixtures
problem: logics/external/modeles-3D/ is gitignored, so the two hand-modelled demo assets exist only on this machine; a fresh clone or CI run falls back to the from-primitives generators and never sees them.
scope_in: Moving both .blend files to a committed path (fixtures/ or equivalent) with author/rights noted wherever the project already records that for committed assets.
Updating both build scripts' default-asset resolution order to check the committed path first.
scope_out: Any change to the assets' own geometry -- that is the render-quality and glass-pane items below.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Both .blend files are tracked in git at a committed path.
AC2: `tools/build_demo_chain.sh` and `tools/build_figurine_chain.sh`, run with no argument on a clean checkout, use the committed asset.

backlog_items.title: Fix the start screen's layout overflow and decide its command affordance
problem: The start screen's three-column layout overflows its own modal at at least one common width.
Its template cards show commands as plain text with no way to run them, even when the page is served.
scope_in: Fixing the overflow, verified with a rendered screenshot at common desktop widths.
A recorded decision (ADR amendment, new ADR, or explicit non-goal) on whether these specific commands become served-runnable, and matching UI either way.
scope_out: Any other viewer layout beyond this modal.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: No column's content pushes past the modal's right edge at common desktop widths.
AC2: A decision is recorded and the start screen's template cards match it.

backlog_items.title: Make report file paths and commands into real, clickable controls
problem: The render panel's 'Open in Blender' command, the Artefact section's written-file path, and other file references throughout the viewer are plain text a person has to select and retype or paste into a terminal by hand.
The File-menu-stays-open-behind-the-splash defect (already fixed inline this session) has no regression coverage.
scope_in: A consistent pattern for file-path and command controls (button or link) applied everywhere the viewer currently prints one, respecting the file://-vs-served distinction already established.
A viewer-smoke assertion that opening the splash from the File menu leaves no menu open behind it.
scope_out: Extending the served command set (covered by the start-screen item above).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The render panel's Blender-open command and the Artefact section's file path are both real controls, not plain text.
AC2: Every other file path the viewer prints follows the same pattern.
AC3: `scripts/viewer_smoke.py` (or equivalent) asserts no `details.menu` stays open after the splash opens from it.

backlog_items.title: Render runbook Markdown as formatted content
problem: The runbook workspace's content pane shows a runbook's raw Markdown source -- headings, lists and code fences all show their literal syntax characters.
scope_in: A small, dependency-free renderer for this project's own runbook Markdown conventions: headings, bullet lists, code fences, inline code, links, bold.
Wiring it into the runbook workspace's content pane.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A runbook opened in the runbook workspace shows formatted headings, lists, code blocks and links -- no literal Markdown syntax visible.
AC2: No new runtime dependency is added.

backlog_items.title: Root-cause the vehicle demonstration's disappearing glass panes
problem: The vehicle asset's glass panes (windshield, side and rear windows) appear to be progressively lost across the demo chain's own operations.
scope_in: Tracing which operation(s) remove or merge the glass panes, using the real chain's own reports.
Either a fix that keeps them intact through the full chain, or an honest, documented explanation in the build script and README if keeping them intact would weaken a real lesson the chain teaches.
scope_out: Any change to the asset's other geometry.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The specific operation(s) responsible are identified and named, with the real report data that shows it.
AC2: Either the panes survive the full chain in a fresh run, or the build script and README explain why not.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver the viewer actionability pass
plan: 1. Commit the two hand-modelled demo assets as fixtures and repoint both build scripts.
2. Fix the start screen's overflow and record the runnable-commands decision.
3. Make report file paths and commands into real controls; add the menu-close regression check.
4. Render runbook Markdown as formatted content.
5. Root-cause and resolve (or honestly document) the vehicle's disappearing glass panes.
6. Re-run make check, fixture_check and viewer_smoke before closeout.
